name: Kapa
summary: A managed retrieval-augmented generation service for technical companies: it keeps an index of your docs, tickets, forums and code in sync and answers questions from it with citations, as an “Ask AI” widget, Slack or Discord bot, support-form deflector, API or MCP server.
intro: You connect sources, such as a docs site, GitHub, Zendesk tickets, Slack channels, Confluence, PDFs or an OpenAPI spec, and Kapa builds one search index from them. The ingestion layer does most of the work: it syncs only what changed, because re-embedding text, converting PDFs and annotating images for every refresh would be too expensive. New and edited content is picked up within minutes for most sources, deletions in a slower pass, Slack’s last seven days are re-scanned because its API cannot report changes, and websites are re-crawled daily, with any crawl that changes or drops a large share of pages held for human review instead of applied.

At question time Kapa retrieves the most relevant chunks and its prebuilt agents write an answer grounded in them, with citations, or say they don’t know. Those agents are deployed with one script tag (the website widget) or as Slack, Discord and Zendesk bots and a support-form deflector, and the questions people ask feed reports on coverage gaps in the docs. Kapa is model-agnostic and uses providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere and Voyage, plus some models of its own.

Developers can skip the prebuilt agents and use only the retrieval: an HTTP endpoint returns ranked chunks with no generation, in a fast `default` mode or a `deep` mode that runs a retrieval agent, and a hosted MCP server at `<subdomain>.mcp.kapa.ai` exposes the same search to Cursor, Claude Code or your own agent. A 14-day trial covers 1 index, 5,000 crawled pages, 5,000 retrieval queries and 1,000 answers; production use is a usage-based Growth plan whose price is quoted on request.
strengths: No RAG pipeline to run: crawling, PDF and image processing, chunking, incremental sync and evals are handled for you
Many surfaces from one index: website widget, Slack, Discord, Zendesk, support form, HTTP API and MCP server
Answers cite their sources, and question analytics show where the documentation is missing or unclear
Retrieval-only use is supported, so you can feed your own agent Kapa’s chunks instead of its answers
limits: Closed and hosted: your content and users’ questions are processed by Kapa and its model providers (with DPAs and training opt-outs), and EU hosting and SSO are Enterprise features
Growth pricing is not published, and the free trial ends after 14 days
Default API limits are 60 retrieval requests and 100 document requests a minute per team
Answer quality depends on your docs: Kapa can only cite what its sources say, and stale or missing pages become “I don’t know” or coverage-gap reports

story: Emil Soerensen and Finn Bauer met in London and did master’s degrees in finance and computer science together; at Imperial College in 2019 they were already experimenting with early embeddings for question answering. In January 2023 two friends running tech companies independently told them the same thing: their support teams were swamped by technical questions their documentation already answered. Early deployments included a Discord bot for LangChain’s community of 30,000 developers.

They built a retrieval-augmented generation stack whose core, they wrote, was crawling infrastructure that keeps the source data current, and launched kapa.ai through Y Combinator’s Summer 2023 batch, with OpenAI, Airbyte and Next.js among early users. In October 2024 they announced a $3.2 million seed round led by Initialized Capital, with angels including the RAG paper co-author Douwe Kiela, Solomon Hykes and Amjad Masad, and more than 100 customers.

By 2026 Kapa was offering its retrieval directly to developers building their own agents, through an API, a hosted MCP server and LangChain and n8n integrations. In October 2026 it released Kapa MCP, which lets Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor set up and run Kapa itself, and published Company Knowledge Bench, a 1,000-question retrieval benchmark built from production data.

choices.why: Embedding, PDF conversion and image annotation cost money per item, so re-indexing whole sources would make even weekly refreshes too expensive; per-source change tracking keeps answers minutes old instead.

choices.choice: Gate website crawls before applying them
choices.why: A redesign or a moved docs tree can silently break a crawl, so a crawl that changes or removes a large share of pages waits for human review rather than corrupting the live index.
The founders saw their success hinge on measuring answer quality, so they test models from several providers against their own evaluations and switch to whichever answers technical questions best.

choices.choice: Answer only from sources, with citations
choices.why: Kapa optimizes for accuracy on technical questions, so answers are grounded in the connected sources, and when those don’t cover a question it says “I don’t know” rather than guessing.
